title: Impact of air pollution on pulmonary function and respiratory symptoms in children. Longitudinal repeated-measures study.
ehr_evidence: The study used a school-based prospective cohort with spirometry and ISAAC questionnaires collected for the study, and ambient air pollutant data provided by the network of atmospheric monitoring of Salamanca (automated environmental monitoring of the Institute of Ecology of the State of Guanajuato).
summary: A longitudinal repeated-measures cohort study of 464 school-age children (6-14 years) from two public schools in Salamanca, Mexico differing in distance from stationary air pollution sources, examining associations of O3, SO2, NO2, and PM10 with pulmonary function and respiratory symptoms.
key_findings: More children from the school closer to pollution sources had lung-function abnormalities than the distant school (17.9% vs 11.5%; p = 0.02).
Obstructive pattern was more frequent in students with greater exposure (10.4% vs 5.3%; OR = 1.95, 95% CI 1.03-3.7).
Mixed pattern was more frequent in the same students (4.1% vs 0.9%; OR = 4.69, 95% CI 1.04-21.1).
A 10 μg/m3 increase in O3 was associated with increased wheezing (OR = 1.0460), rhinorrhea (OR = 1.0429), ARTI (OR = 1.0820), and dyspnea (OR = 1.0313).
A 10 μg/m3 increase in PM10 was associated with wheezing (OR = 1.0478), rhinorrhea (OR = 1.0318), ARTI (OR = 1.0977), and dyspnea (OR = 1.0184).
A 10 μg/m3 increase in SO2 was associated with wheezing (OR = 1.0213) and ARTI (OR = 1.0521).
No significant effects were observed with NO2.
Asthma (22.5% vs 9.7%; p = 0.0005), rhinitis (44.7% vs 34.2%; p = 0.01), and eczema (13.3% vs 4.4%; p = 0.001) were more frequent in the closer school.
An IQR increase in PM10 (18.8 μg/m3) was associated with 3-month FEV1 deficits of -0.37% in girls and -0.43% in boys and PEF deficits of -0.29% in girls and -0.36% in boys.
There was no consistent effect of air pollution levels on symptom rates or lung function.
captured_features: FVC, FEV1, FEV1/FVC, PEF spirometric values
respiratory symptoms (wheezing, rhinorrhea, eczema, acute respiratory tract infections, dyspnea, hospitalization)
ambient pollutant levels (O3, SO2, NO, NO2, NOx, PM10)
socioeconomic status, atopy, fossil fuel use, passive smoking
pathologies_diseases: reduced pulmonary function / obstructive, restrictive, and mixed lung-function abnormalities
population: 464 school-age children aged 6-14 years from two public schools in Salamanca, Guanajuato, Mexico
exposure_domain: air pollution (O3, SO2, NO2, PM10, CO, NO, NOx)
limitations: Lack of a non-polluted control area.
Results cannot be generalized due to the particular environmental and geographic features of the city.
Potential confounding and multi-collinearity among air pollution and meteorological variables.
Unmeasured characteristics such as natural allergens, other pollutants, seasonal viral infections, and genetic predisposition.
